tagline: Up to the big trees, then down into the canyon.
intro: Highway 180 sets out from the western foothills of the Sierra Nevada at about 2,000 feet, near Dunlap, where the stagecoaches once stopped to change horses. It climbs through oak chaparral and pine and fir forest to 6,500 feet and the General Grant Grove, where a short walk reaches the second-largest giant sequoia in the world.
Then the road turns down, 2,700 feet to the Kings River, past Junction View, Marble Mountain View and Grizzly Falls. It is the only road into Kings Canyon, and it ends just past Cedar Grove.
season: Mid-May to mid-October, when the road into the canyon is open.

moments.title: Wilsonia
moments.text: A cabin village inside Grant Grove, named for Woodrow Wilson because California's mountain votes, held up by a snowstorm, decided his reelection in 1916.

moments.title: Boyden Cavern
moments.text: Below the 2,000-foot marble walls of the Portals of the Kings, guided tours go down past a flowstone called Mother Nature's Wedding Cake to a small underground stream.

moments.title: Cedar Grove
moments.text: John Muir called it Deer Park in 1891. A hotel went up here without a permit in 1897 and was made to close the next year. The incense cedars stayed.

practical: The road from below the Hume Lake turnoff to Roads End closes in winter, typically November to April.
